summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of polymyositis, diastolic heart failure, morbid obesity, and anticoagulation for prior clots was admitted for worsening shortness of breath and fluid overload after being unable to access her medications due to a broken scooter. She had stopped her medications, including warfarin and diuretics, for several weeks. She was treated with IV diuresis, which improved her respiratory status and reduced her weight from 223.2 kg to 211.8 kg. Her INR was initially 1.0, so she was bridged with heparin and restarted on warfarin, reaching a therapeutic INR of 2.1 by discharge. Due to deconditioning and steroid-related adrenal suppression, she was evaluated by physical therapy and discharged to inpatient rehab. Her diabetes was managed with insulin in the hospital, and metformin was restarted at discharge. She was transitioned from IV lasix to oral torsemide and continued all home immunosuppressive and supportive therapies.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Lung involvement in other diseases classified elsewhere
